O.content: The blue line descends from near the 0 tick at the left to below the 8000 tick at the right.
The y-axis label is "Count," while its printed numeric ticks increase from 0 at the top to 8000 lower on the page.

B.text: If the vertical axis instead follows ordinary upward-increasing quantity encoding despite its printed tick ordering, then the rightward downward line would indicate easing demand, which would support step-down recovery planning.
B.conditions: Applies only if the printed y-axis labels are not the operative value mapping.

O.content: The title reads "Month vs. Number of COVID-19 patients hospitalized"; the horizontal axis is labeled "Month" and the vertical axis is labeled "Count".
Visible date labels run from "Feb 24, 2020" at the left to "Mar 14, 2020" at the right.
The printed y-axis ticks show 0 near the top, then 2000, 4000, 6000, and 8000 at progressively lower positions.
The blue line and markers descend sharply toward the right; the final marker is below the 8000 tick and the preceding recent markers span between the 4000, 6000, and 8000 tick levels.

B.text: If the plotted series is the COVID-19 hospitalized-patient count over time, the x-axis progresses from earlier dates at left to later dates at right, and the y-axis numeric labels increase downward, then a line moving downward toward the right indicates increasing inpatient census. If the current-period increase is rapid, route to surge-capacity planning guidance.
B.conditions: Applies to the single visible COVID-19 hospitalization series and treats the rightmost date as the current period; 'rapidly increasing' is assessed from the visibly steep recent segment.
